oracle.tool: tools/c-oracle (libclang, verdict from clang's own diagnostic categories)
oracle.note: THREE-VALUED: valid / invalid / indeterminate, the only oracle that is. See crates/treebank-c/ORACLE.md; the claim is 'no syntax error, in GNU C, given these include paths', NOT 'this compiles'. Lang::validate collapses indeterminate to false, so gap_files is a FLOOR. This is the language that proves `flags` has to exist: -std=gnu17 selects the dialect and the libclang version alone does not settle it. The include-path flags are per-file and are described in corpus.oracle_flags rather than here.

smoke.note: No `requires`: c-oracle needs libclang headers to BUILD, which build.sh reports on, and nothing on PATH to run.

corpus.source: Debian sid, source packages ranked by popcon (popularity-contest) installs aggregated per source package, filtered to packages whose sources.debian.org SLOC is >=2000 ansic and ansic >= cpp; upstream .orig.tar.* only (never the .debian.tar.* patch tarball); .c and .h files, C++ headers excluded by content
corpus.source_note: C has no registry, so popularity is borrowed. popcon counts machines, which is closer in kind to crates.io downloads than Java's dependent-repos proxy. The bias is explicit and it is the point: this corpus is the C that ships in a distribution — system libraries, daemons, autotools trees, GNU extensions — NOT trending C on GitHub, which is a different corpus and would give different gap numbers. The SLOC filter exists because popcon ranks everything Debian ships: without it the top of the list spends its bandwidth on LibreOffice (4.4M lines of C++ to 34k of C) and gcc-16 (no C at all).
corpus.oracle: tools/c-oracle — libclang 20.1.2, parse-only, verdict from clang's own diagnostic categories. THREE-VALUED: valid / invalid / indeterminate. See crates/treebank-c/ORACLE.md for what it does and does not claim; the short version is 'no syntax error, in GNU C, given these include paths', NOT 'this compiles'. Lang::validate collapses indeterminate to false, so gap_files is a FLOOR and noise_files mixes 'reference rejected it' with 'could not tell'; the full split is in corpus/c/oracle-verdicts.json and on the sweep's stderr.
corpus.fetched: 2026-08-11 (popcon + sid Sources snapshot of that date)
corpus.files_note: .c and .h from the top 100 C source packages by popcon; C++ headers excluded by content (unguarded namespace/template/class, comments and __cplusplus-guarded regions excluded from the scan)

oracle_split.note: of the 40,434 files still failing with patches 0003-0015 applied (corpus/c/oracle-verdicts.json, written by the same sweep). INDETERMINATE STILL OUTNUMBERS VALID 1.6:1, so gap_files is a floor and noise_files mixes 'reference rejected it' (652) with 'could not tell' (24,694). ~79% of indeterminates carry an unresolved include, but that is not what makes them indeterminate: valid requires parse == 0, so a missing header never prevents a valid verdict and resolving one cannot produce it. Stubbing the configure-generated config.h — the obvious idea, and one this ledger used to recommend — is structurally incapable of helping and can only manufacture 'invalid' verdicts; measured, 0 of 500 indeterminate files change verdict with a stub, and 118 of 11,983 would flip the wrong way. See ORACLE.md, 'Stubbing config.h cannot work'.

corpus.oracle_flags: -std=gnu17 -ferror-limit=0 -w, -iquote<every header-bearing dir in the package and its ancestors>, -I<package root, include/, inc/, src/, lib/>, -idirafter<every header-bearing dir>
corpus.oracle_flags_note: Three search paths, each doing a distinct job. -iquote answers the package's own quoted includes. -I is limited to the package's PUBLIC dirs on purpose: it is searched before the system dirs, so a wide -I list lets a package's private replacements for system headers shadow the real ones (glibc string/string.h answering <string.h>) and resolution gets WORSE (measured: 4578 -> 4060 valid). -idirafter carries the wide list instead; being searched AFTER the system dirs it can only supply headers the system lacks, which is what glibc's <sigsetops.h> needs. Measured on 1,500 failing files: -iquote+public -I alone = 372 valid / 11 invalid / 1117 indeterminate; adding -idirafter = 453 / 37 / 1010.

top_gap_clusters.class: statement macro followed by a block, e.g. list_for_each(li, &q->ifaces) { ... }
extern "C" brace asymmetry: `{` inside one #ifdef __cplusplus and `}` inside another. Preprocessor-inherent, same shape as the C# asymmetry; not a fixable grammar bug
undefined macro in declaration position, e.g. _INLINE_ void __list_add(...)
macro in declaration position, e.g. THREAD_LOCAL int adjustment = 0;
type as a macro argument, e.g. list_entry(a, struct file_element, file_list)

corpus.oracle_correction: The first published numbers for this corpus (gap 5629, invalid 302, indeterminate 12006) were computed while c-oracle had a fixed 128-flag cap per request, which silently truncated the include list for the three largest packages — glibc alone has 498 header-bearing dirs. The cap is gone; the numbers above are the corrected ones. The truncation also made -idirafter look inert, because its flags were the ones being dropped.
corpus.source_freshness: rank re-downloads the sid Sources index when the cached copy is older than 12h (TREEBANK_REFRESH_SOURCES=1 forces it). The index carries every package's version, so a permanently cached copy froze the corpus: resolve() would return the same tarballs forever, the sweep cache would skip them all, and the 'new version of a top-K package' event this loop is built on could never fire for C. The per-package SLOC verdicts are cached in corpus/c/db/sloc.json keyed by name and stamped with the version measured, so a daily re-rank queries only the packages whose version moved — measured at k=200: 227 lookups in 9s cold (~25/sec, 8-way), then 2 lookups and 1.9s warm. sources.debian.org lags the archive, so a version it has not indexed yet falls back to the newest it does hold; without that, a refresh on an upload day silently dropped glibc and mesa, the two largest C sources in the corpus.
corpus.preprocessing: crates/treebank-preprocessing, declared via Lang::preprocessing(): __cplusplus is undefined when parsing C. The sweep re-parses each VALID failing file with dead branches removed; the 909 that then parse cleanly are recorded as config_files rather than gaps, because no grammar patch can fix them — a header opening `extern "C" {` inside one #ifdef __cplusplus and closing `}` inside another has no single well-formed tree. Without this they sat at #2 in the fix queue, the largest cluster an agent could not win. A second pass forces individual conditional branches: where the symbol is unknown (#ifdef F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC around one of two spellings of a signature) it does not matter what the symbol means, because both branches are valid and the grammar fails only on seeing both. 51 more files are explained entirely this way and 43 are re-clustered onto the problem that was hiding behind a split. The soundness guard is that the error's own line must survive the forcing — without it an include guard 'clears' every error in a header by emptying it, which accounted for 173 of 243 raw hits.
corpus.macro_diagnosis: crates/treebank-preprocessing expands the package's macros into each gap file and re-parses. on the 20-package pilot, 1,102 of the 4,593 gap files (24.0%) then parsed cleanly, so the grammar was meeting an unexpanded macro rather than unfamiliar syntax. This does NOT change the verdict — unlike the extern "C" case, THREAD_LOCAL int x; is something a grammar could parse — it annotates each cluster with the macros responsible (SPA_EXPORT, drm_public, _PUBLIC_, DBUS_EXPORT, NCURSES_CONST, weak_alias...), which is what writing a minimal rule and judging its over-acceptance needs.
corpus.sweep_note: Both numbers are the 100-package corpus above (84,455 files). The 20-package pilot these fields used to carry (39,928 files, 21,991 passed) is kept in LOCAL-PATCHES.md under 'Pilot sweep — measured', with the include-flag and oracle experiments that were run on it; the pair here has to be comparable, so it moves with the corpus. sweep_patched is patches 0003-0015 applied.
corpus.negative_corpus: 15 files, each rejected by the oracle AND by the grammar. Six were added by adversarial review of the thirteen-fix sweep PR, which introduced thirteen permissive rules and no new guards: a malformed case range at either end, a bit-field with no width, typeof with no operand, _Atomic with no type, and a type descriptor used where a value belongs. Each one is the boundary a new rule must not cross.

patches.title: anonymous bit-fields
patches.origin: treebank; found by the Debian sid popcon sweep

evidence.diagnosis: C11 6.7.2.1 writes struct-declarator as `declarator` or `declarator_opt : constant-expression`, so a bit-field may be unnamed: `unsigned int :3;` is padding and `int :0;` forces alignment to the next storage unit. _field_declaration_declarator required a declarator before bitfield_clause, so every such member parsed as MISSING field_identifier. The rule is now the two-way choice the standard writes.

patches.title: GNU attributes in declaration positions
patches.origin: treebank; found by the Debian sid popcon sweep

evidence.diagnosis: Three positions GCC accepts and the grammar did not: after the declarator of an object declaration, after the `*` of a pointer declarator, and on either side of the type in a typedef. The first is a new rule, gnu_attributed_declarator, aliased back to attributed_declarator so the node name is unchanged, and limited to the object declarators on purpose: function declarators, parameters, fields and typedefs already absorb a trailing attribute, and letting the general attributed_declarator take __attribute__ made all four ambiguous — generation failed on three of them, and with the conflict declared, `void f(int x __attribute__((unused)))` re-parsed into a different tree and broke upstream's own Attributes and Type qualifiers corpus tests.
evidence.sweep_note: measured for patches 0004-0013 as a stack: a full sweep of this corpus is 84,455 files and ~45 minutes, almost all of it the reference parser adjudicating the 41k failures, so the eleven fixes were developed and corpus-tested one at a time and swept together. sweep_before is the tree with 0003 applied, sweep_after the whole series.

patches.title: named variadic macro parameters
patches.origin: treebank; found by the Debian sid popcon sweep

evidence.repro:
#define check(FMT...) do { } while (0)
#define log(fmt, args...) printf(fmt, ##args)
evidence.diagnosis: `#define check(FMT...)` is the GNU spelling of a variadic macro: the parameter name stands for the rest of the argument list where ISO C writes `...` and __VA_ARGS__. preproc_params took `identifier` or `...` but not an identifier carrying one, so the whole #define was an error.

patches.title: complex types
patches.origin: treebank; found by the Debian sid popcon sweep

evidence.diagnosis: _Complex and _Imaginary (C99 6.7.2) appear beside float/double rather than instead of them, which is why they belong with signed/unsigned/long/short in sized_type_specifier and not in primitive_type. __complex__ is GCC's spelling. Without them `_Complex float cf;` read as two juxtaposed type names and failed.

patches.title: __has_include in preprocessor conditionals
patches.origin: treebank; found by the Debian sid popcon sweep

evidence.diagnosis: __has_include is C23 and a GNU/clang extension long before it. Its operand is a header name, not an expression, so like `defined` it cannot go through preproc_call_expression — the <...> form is a system_lib_string, which inside an #if would otherwise lex as a less-than operator. New preproc_has_include node, mirroring preproc_defined.

patches.title: typeof
patches.origin: treebank; found by the Debian sid popcon sweep

evidence.diagnosis: C23's typeof, spelled __typeof/__typeof__ by GCC for decades. typeof(x) on a bare name already parsed by accident, as a macro_type_specifier whose operand looked like a type descriptor; anything else did not, because no type descriptor holds a field access. The new typeof_specifier takes either a type or an expression.

patches.title: _Atomic type specifier
patches.origin: treebank; found by the Debian sid popcon sweep

evidence.diagnosis: C11 6.7.2.4 gives _Atomic two jobs: the qualifier `_Atomic int x;`, which the grammar had, and the atomic type specifier `_Atomic(int) x;`, which it did not. mimalloc, vendored inside CPython, is written in the second form throughout.

patches.title: a label at the end of a compound statement
patches.origin: treebank; found by the Debian sid popcon sweep

evidence.diagnosis: C23 6.8.1 allows a label with no statement after it at the end of a block — the `out:` the `goto out;` idiom leaves before the closing brace — and GCC and clang accept it in every dialect. labeled_statement required a statement, so the block ended with a MISSING ;. trailing_label is admitted only in that one position, so a label with no statement stays an error anywhere else.

patches.title: a type as a call argument when it carries an abstract declarator
patches.origin: treebank; found by the Debian sid popcon sweep

evidence.diagnosis: va_arg is a macro and its second argument is a type, not an expression; the same shape appears throughout the corpus in package-local macros. argument_list already admits a compound_statement for exactly this reason (upstream's note: macros taking statements as arguments), and this extends it to a type descriptor — but only one carrying an abstract declarator (`char *`, `int (*)(void)`, `long []`), none of which can be read as an expression. A bare type name is not accepted, so test/negative/type-in-plain-call-argument.c (`g(struct s)`) stays rejected. Nor is a leading qualifier: making `const` valid at the start of an argument makes the lexer prefer the keyword inside __attribute__((const)) and breaks upstream's Attributes test, so `va_arg(ap, const char *)` still fails while `char const *` parses. The alias carries prec.dynamic(-2) so macro_type_specifier keeps winning where upstream's tests say it should.
evidence.sweep_note: measured for patches 0004-0013 as a stack: a full sweep of this corpus is 84,455 files and ~45 minutes, almost all of it the reference parser adjudicating the 41k failures, so the eleven fixes were developed and corpus-tested one at a time and swept together. sweep_before is the tree with 0003 applied, sweep_after the whole series.
evidence.known_over_acceptance: Deliberate and inherent: allowing `va_arg(ap, char *)` means `g(char *)` parses too, and that is invalid C when g is a function rather than a macro. Nothing in the token stream distinguishes them. Confirmed by adversarial review: the oracle calls `int g(int); int f(void) { return g(char *); }` invalid (1 parse issue) and the grammar accepts it. The boundary that IS held is a bare type name — test/negative/type-in-plain-call-argument.c pins `g(struct s)` as rejected, and type-descriptor-is-not-an-expression.c pins `(char *)` as a value.

patches.title: preprocessor directives between enumerators
patches.origin: treebank; found by the Debian sid popcon sweep

evidence.diagnosis: enumerator_list already admitted #if/#ifdef and a bare #directive, but not #define — and the kernel UAPI headers (which systemd vendors wholesale) put a #define after every enumerator so each name is testable with #ifdef. Unlike an enumerator the directive is not followed by a comma, and it can also follow the last enumerator, so it needed a slot in both the repeat and the comma-less tail.
evidence.sweep_note: measured for patches 0014-0015 as a pair: sweep_before is the tree with 0003-0013 applied, sweep_after the whole series.

patches.title: preprocessor conditionals and directives in an initializer list
patches.origin: treebank; found by the Debian sid popcon sweep

evidence.diagnosis: A braced initializer whose elements are guarded by #ifdef is one of the commonest shapes in this corpus — tables of syscalls, ioctls, partition types, colour names — and initializer_list was a plain commaSep with no preprocessor slot at all, so the whole declaration failed. It is now shaped like enumerator_list: element-then-comma, or a conditional, or a directive, with the same comma-less tail. preprocIf gets two more instantiations, _in_initializer_list and _in_initializer_list_no_comma, which is exactly how upstream already handles enumerators and struct members. The #include slot is for the list-fragment header (util-linux's pt-mbr-partnames.h), which stays invalid on its own — test/negative/ still rejects the fragment itself. The one new conflict, [expression, concatenated_string], is the identifier-then-string ambiguity concatenated_string has always carried, reachable now that an #ifdef name can sit directly before an element.
evidence.sweep_note: measured for patches 0014-0015 as a pair: sweep_before is the tree with 0003-0013 applied, sweep_after the whole series.
